implementation_state: All four gates are met and both named defects are repaired, so this moves off FAILED; it stays PARTIAL rather than DONE because nothing in the application calls the rollback path yet. Conflict resolution being disconnected from release was repaired by I3's release_resolved, not here: resolve_conflicts had computed a resolution with no production caller since before either node was touched. The rollback defect was that MigrationResult reported state RolledBack and rolled_back true whether or not a byte went back, with restore failures pushed into warnings, errors hardcoded empty and rolled_back a constant -- so a rollback that restored nothing was indistinguishable from a clean one to every caller. rolled_back now answers whether the pre-migration state was actually put back and is false whenever any restore failed, with restored_files and failed_restores naming which file went which way. The restore failure is injected through SnapshotWriter rather than provoked with read-only permissions, because CI runs Linux, macOS and Windows and read-only semantics differ between them; a gate whose outcome depends on the OS is green until it is not. Restore failures are recorded in errors and not only in warnings, because every caller checks errors.is_empty() and none are obliged to read warnings.
unblock_condition: Close I2 and I3 contracts and pass conflict-safe restore/rollback tests with explicit failure reporting.
notes: The audit decision was preserved as FAILED and is now superseded: the conditions the audit recorded were repaired, and blocked_by is empty because I2 and I3 no longer name an unresolved gate. The status is PARTIAL, not DONE, because no production caller exists.

Whether a dependency's gates being met is what satisfies an edge, or whether the dependency must additionally be INTEGRATED, is answered by the DAG's own rule rather than by preference: blocked_by is defined as a subset of dependencies naming an active unresolved gate. It keys on gates, so met and verified gates close the contract.
